bug_semantics: Nokogiri's CSS selector tokenizer (lib/nokogiri/css/tokenizer.rex, generated lib/nokogiri/css/tokenizer.rb) compiles CSS-2.1-style macros to Onigmo/Joni regular expressions. Three exponential-backtracking (CWE-1333) vectors share nested alternation under '*' plus {unicode}'s variable-length hex run \[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6}. (1) STRING: the body class [^\n\r\f"] also matches '\', overlapping the {escape} branch, so unterminated input like [foo="\a\a\a... has 2**N parses. (2) STRING: each hex-escape position admits six lengths, so \aaaaaa\aaaaaa... has 6**N parses; missing the closing quote forces the engine to enumerate every parse before failing. (3) IDENT/FUNCTION: the same {1,6} length ambiguity sits under {nmchar}* in {ident}; when {ident}\({w} fails because no '(' follows an identifier-shaped prefix, payload \aaaaaa\aaaaaa...X backtracks through 6**N parses (n=10 ~11.4s). Attackers inject adversarial selectors into Nokogiri::CSS.xpath_for, Node#css, Node#at_css, Searchable#search, or CSS::Parser#parse. Affected: nokogiri < 1.19.3. Patched: 1.19.3, which wraps the STRING/nmchar/nmstart bodies in atomic groups (?>...) and excludes '\' from the string class.
flaw_origin: The first CSS tokenizer, 9246422c850b9e580eead224fd17ed5ff5564878 (Aaron Patterson, 2008-09-17, 'adding tokenizer and parser'), copied the W3C CSS 2.1 lexical grammar into rex/frex macros: unicode \[0-9a-f]{1,6}..., escape using {unicode}, nmchar/nmstart using {escape}, string1/string2 with ({...{escape}})* and a required closing quote, and a {ident}\( FUNCTION rule. Those constructions are safe-ish as flex rules but become ReDoS when expanded to Ruby regexes. Same-day follow-up c06a48ae7d4e01f51e1a7a8924b93f55e3fa253b dropped '\\' from the string negated class, creating Vector 1's cross-branch overlap (the spec class is [^\n\r\f\\"]). 4ba1df8e45b9813048d201c8a4e7e56a09aa1079 later added (?<!\\)(?:\\{2})* only as bookkeeping for that overlap. 3d3238c3650cf1649731fc6ff8f30ef767e3a245 regrouped macros but did not first write the mechanism. The 2026 fix (GHSA-c4rq-3m3g-8wgx / PR #3626, v1.19.x backport #3627) is atomic grouping plus restoring the backslash exclusion.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-79770 / GHSA-5jhf-fpp7-v2pv is a real, published ReDoS in Nokogiri's CSS tokenizer, matching first-party GHSA-c4rq-3m3g-8wgx (not withdrawn; CVE.org/VulnCheck state=PUBLISHED). The sink is the rexical tokenizer used by Node#css / at_css / Searchable#search / CSS.xpath_for. The flawed mechanism is CSS-2.1 unicode/escape/string/ident macros compiled to backtracking Ruby regexes: {1,6} hex-escape length nested under *, plus (for Vector 1) a string class that also consumes backslash. BIC search used git log -L on tokenizer.rex string1/unicode/nmchar and -S on the ident/FUNCTION rules, then parent-tree verification. 9246422c850b9e580eead224fd17ed5ff5564878 is the smallest public commit that first wrote those macros; its parent 09f133def133eb8c80dd003bf1c70205836f7237 has no tokenizer files, so introducer_parent_absent=false. It is not a move, refactor, revert, backport, or squash. Later c06a48ae (Vector 1 class change), 4ba1df8e (lookbehind), and 3d3238c3 (paren regrouping) modify already-vulnerable lines and are not BICs. Tag check: BIC is in v1.19.2 (affected) and every earlier release tag that contains the tokenizer; the complete 1.19.3 fix is backport merge 7501a63b (#3627), whose first content commit 00926231 is the cherry-pick of the STRING-rule fix (vectors 1-2); ident vector 3 follows in b984b7e4.
